case.case_title: Jinadasa v. Associated Newspapers of Ceylon Ltd.
case.source_citation: Supreme Court of Sri Lanka, S.C. FR No. 296/98, decided on 12 November 1998

clause.text: No citizen shall be discriminated against on the grounds of race, religion, language, caste, sex, political opinion, place of birth or any one of such grounds.

case_context.legal_issue: Whether the petitioner was discriminated against on prohibited grounds in violation of Article 12(2) of the Constitution.
case_context.petitioner_claim: The petitioner alleged discrimination violating Article 12(2).
case_context.respondent_argument: The respondents denied any discrimination, noting the petitioner’s promotions and salary increments under the present government and commendations from the Chairman.
key_facts: Petitioner was promoted and given salary increments under the present government.
The present Chairman gave the petitioner a letter of commendation in 1997.
No evidence was presented to show discrimination on any prohibited grounds.

reasoning.interpretation_summary: The court considered Article 12(2) protects against discrimination on specified grounds and requires evidence of such discrimination.
reasoning.application_to_facts: The court found no evidence that the petitioner was discriminated against on any prohibited ground; his promotions and commendations under the current government negated claims of discrimination.

outcome.holding: The court held that there was no violation of Article 12(2) as no discrimination was proven.

link_explanation.why_this_clause_matters: Article 12(2) was considered to assess claims of discrimination but was ultimately found not to be violated due to lack of evidence.

evidence.evidence_excerpt: The petitioner’s promotions and salary increments under the present government and a commendation letter from the Chairman showed no evidence of discrimination.
